clue.text: Home of the silly brash parasite in family, daughter

indicators.note: in places the brash parasite inside the word for family

parts.note: a clan is an extended family
brash means loud
the cuckoo is a brood parasite, laying its eggs in other birds' nests

explanation.surface: A noisy cuckoo living with a family and their daughter makes for a silly household.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Home of the silly' reads like a jibe at the family, but it is the definition; 'in' puts the brash parasite inside the family word.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloud cuckoo land is an idiom for a fantasy realm of absurd, unrealistic thinking, where foolish people dwell.

clue.text: Garment a minister pulled up in open-topped car

indicators.note: in sets the turned-round pieces inside the shortened car
open-topped means the car word loses its top, its first letter in a down clue

parts.note: a Rolls is a Rolls-Royce car

indicators.note: pulled up, in a down clue, means the letters read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a minister of religion

explanation.surface: A clergyman is hauled up into a convertible car while wearing something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulled up' turns A REV into VERA; 'open-topped' strips the top letter from the car, leaving OLLS, which takes VERA 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Overalls are a loose protective garment worn over ordinary clothes for dirty work.

clue.text: Every other bit extracted, darker gas remains

indicators.note: every other bit extracted means the alternate letters of darker gas are lifted out, starting with the first

explanation.surface: Taking out alternate bits of a darker gas leaves some residue behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Dregs are the sediment left at the bottom of a vessel, the remains after the liquid has gone.

clue.text: Leader of men stepped up with German champions

indicators.note: up, in a down clue, makes the word for stepped read from bottom to top

parts.note: trod is the past tense of tread, to step

indicators.note: leader of points to the first letter of men

parts.note: und is German for and, which here stands in for with

explanation.surface: A leader of men climbs onto the podium with the German champions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns TROD into DORT; M is the 'Leader of' men. 'German' looks like part of the definition, but it signals the foreign word for 'with'.
explanation.definitionFit: Borussia Dortmund won the European Champions League in 1997, so the club counts among past champions.

clue.text: Champions not needing extra time, man — game of two halves, perhaps?

indicators.note: not needing says the letters for extra time are dropped from the club name

parts.note: Celtic, the Glasgow club, won the European Cup in 1967
ET is the usual abbreviation for extra time in football
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A football report: champions won without extra time, and a man trots out the old line about a game of two halves.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing ET from CELTIC leaves CLIC. The definition is an example, hence 'perhaps?'.
explanation.definitionFit: 'It's a game of two halves' is a notoriously overused football commentators' saying, a stock example of a hackneyed phrase.

clue.text: Champions stuffed, striker choked up

indicators.note: choked means the word for stuffed has something wedged in its middle

parts.note: stuffed, as with food, means fed

indicators.note: up, in a down clue, reads the striker's name from bottom to top

parts.note: Wayne Rooney was England's record-scoring striker

explanation.surface: A beaten team is fed up, and their striker choked in front of goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the striker's name round to YENOOR, and 'choked' wedges it into the word for stuffed. Wayne Rooney is England's former record goalscorer.
explanation.definitionFit: Feyenoord of Rotterdam won the European Cup in 1970, becoming the first Dutch club to be crowned champions.

clue.text: Risk chaining animal, dog

indicators.note: chaining means holding something within, as a chain restrains an animal

parts.note: to risk money is to bet
an ass is a donkey

explanation.surface: It's a risk tying up an animal next to a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The basset is a short-legged hound breed with long ears, used for hunting by scent.

clue.text: Outgoing leader old and new on throne better

indicators.note: new tells you the letters of old and are made fresh, in a different order

parts.note: the throne and the john are both slang for the toilet
to trump is to better or beat, as with a higher card

explanation.surface: An old leader and a new one, and which of them sits on the throne better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges OLD AND into DONALD; 'on' simply joins the pieces. The clue appeared as the 2020 US president was leaving office.
explanation.definitionFit: The 45th US president was on his way out of the White House when this puzzle ran in January 2021.

clue.text: Champions can win without a back

indicators.note: back means the whole sequence is read in reverse

parts.note: can is slang for the toilet, as is loo

indicators.note: without means the a is left out of the word for win

parts.note: to prevail is to win

explanation.surface: Champions who lack a defender at the back can still win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' drops A from the word for win, giving PREVIL; 'back' then turns the whole string LOOPREVIL round. 'Can' is slang for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Liverpool have won the European Cup six times and were reigning English league champions when this ran.

clue.text: Inspiration for writing part of plot, a reprobate in hindsight

indicators.note: in hindsight says the hidden letters are read backwards
part of says the answer is a portion of the letters of the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something inspired the writing of part of a plot featuring a scoundrel, seen looking back.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft folded 'part' into the definition, leaving the hidden word with no signal; 'part of' is the hiding indicator, so the definition is 'Inspiration for writing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is the Greek Muse of lyric and love poetry, a source of inspiration to poets.

clue.text: Post over on one side

parts.note: time is up when it is over
right is one side, as opposed to left

explanation.surface: A post leaning over to one side.
explanation.definitionFit: An upright is a vertical post, such as either of the goalposts in rugby.

clue.text: Champions from west side of capital cutting ace, surprisingly

indicators.note: cutting means the capital's fragment slices into the jumbled letters
surprisingly means the letters of ace turn up in an unexpected order
west side of keeps the left half of the city name, as it reads across

parts.note: Helsinki is the capital of Finland

explanation.surface: A team from the west side of the capital somehow serves up an ace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' tempts you to London, where Chelsea play, but it is Helsinki: its 'west side' HELS cuts into CEA, the letters of ACE shuffled ('surprisingly').
explanation.definitionFit: Chelsea won the Champions League in 2012, so the London club are former European champions.

clue.text: See 21
Jerk refused, too confident

indicators.note: a jerk is a sudden jolt, which shakes these letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone refused with a jerk, too sure of themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Sure-footed literally means steady on one's feet, and figuratively confident and unlikely to err.

clue.text: Champions behind, tale-teller almost nets

indicators.note: nets means catches inside, as a net traps a fish
almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: the Miller tells a tale in Chaucer's Canterbury Tales
arse is British slang for the behind, the backside

explanation.surface: Champions trail behind while a teller of tall tales nearly scores.
explanation.walkthrough: MILLE (MILLER, 'almost') 'nets' ARSE, the British word for backside.
explanation.definitionFit: Olympique de Marseille won the Champions League in 1993, the only French club to do so.

clue.text: Apple ending in mud behind second player?

indicators.note: behind means the final letter of mud comes after the player

parts.note: a co-star is a second leading player sharing top billing

indicators.note: ending in picks the final letter of mud

explanation.surface: A supporting actor ends up in the mud behind someone.
explanation.definitionFit: The costard is an old English variety of large cooking apple, the source of the word costermonger.

clue.text: Wrap sticker and ring around it

indicators.note: around means the sticker and ring together enclose the word it

parts.note: a burr is a prickly seed case that sticks to clothing
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Instructions for wrapping: a sticker and a ring go around it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrap' doubles as the definition: a burrito is itself a wrap. 'around' sets the sticker and ring on either side of IT.
explanation.definitionFit: A burrito is a Mexican dish of filling rolled up in a tortilla, like a wrap sandwich.

clue.text: See 25
Rest privy to captivating opening scenes

indicators.note: captivating means holding captive, so the opening scenes go inside

parts.note: to be privy to a secret is to be in on it
Act I contains the opening scenes of a play

explanation.surface: Rest is a privilege of those in on the opening scenes, which captivate.
explanation.definitionFit: Inaction is a state of doing nothing, the same idea as rest or idleness.

clue.text: Work and work to guard against endless excess

indicators.note: to guard means to surround protectively, so the shortened word sits inside

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: endless means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: versus means against
to ply a trade is to work at it

explanation.surface: Work and more work guard against having too much.
explanation.walkthrough: OP 'to guard' VERSU (VERSUS made 'endless'), then PLY.
explanation.definitionFit: An oversupply is a glut, more of something than is needed.

clue.text: Number serious, though first ignored

indicators.note: first ignored means the opening letter is left off the word for serious

parts.note: a weighty matter is a serious one

explanation.surface: A number that is serious, though its first part is overlooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Eighty is a number, eight tens.

clue.text: Where one might stop champions, club and everything?

parts.note: FC Porto won the European Cup in 1987 and the Champions League in 2004
FC stands for Football Club
all means everything

explanation.surface: A wondering where champions, club and the whole lot might be halted.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs from 21 down into 13 across.
explanation.definitionFit: A port of call is a place visited on a journey, a stopping point.

clue.text: Old Hindu in a jiffy?

indicators.note: the question mark owns up that only the first letter of jiffy is meant, as J is the initial

explanation.surface: Someone asks if an ancient Indian believer could be found in no time at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'in a j(iffy)': J, A and IN, rearranged into answer order.
explanation.definitionFit: Jainism is an ancient Indian faith, and a Jain is a follower of it, loosely grouped with Hindus.

clue.text: Dress a start in audition?

indicators.note: in audition means as heard spoken, a sound-alike signal

parts.note: a dawn is a start, the beginning of the day

explanation.surface: Is the costume an opening at an audition?
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent A DAWN and ADORN sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: To adorn is to decorate or embellish, much as to dress a shop window or a dish.

clue.text: Classic saint securing soldier with longer pins

indicators.note: securing means holding fast within, so the soldier goes inside

parts.note: the St Leger, named after Anthony St Leger, is one of Britain's five Classic horse races
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A famous horse race takes in a soldier whose legs are longer.
explanation.walkthrough: The St Leger is a British Classic flat horse race at Doncaster; LEGER holds GI.
explanation.definitionFit: Pins is slang for legs, so having longer pins means being leggier.

clue.text: Champions rise up, status inspiring hero after header from defender

indicators.note: inspiring means breathing in, so the rebel word takes the other pieces inside

parts.note: to rebel is to rise up against authority

indicators.note: after puts the hero following the defender's first letter
header from takes the first letter of defender

parts.note: a star is a hero, a celebrity
grade is rank or status

explanation.surface: Champions rise up; their standing inspires a hero following a defender's header.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inspiring' (breathing in) puts D, the 'header from' defender, with the hero 'after' it, inside the word for rise up; status follows. The answer runs from 25 across into 17 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Red Star Belgrade, Crvena Zvezda of Serbia, won the European Cup in 1991.

clue.text: Birth needing attention then after labour, primarily

definitions.note: a noun defining an adjective meaning relating to birth

indicators.note: primarily means take the primary, first letter of each word

explanation.surface: A birth needing attention after labour.
explanation.definitionFit: Natal is the adjective of birth, as in natal day or antenatal care.

clue.text: Cryptically create from document sent to vendor

indicators.note: cryptically says the answer must be read as a crossword instruction

parts.note: read as an instruction, the answer tells you to put the letters of form in order, which creates from

explanation.surface: A document sent to a vendor is a way of having something created.
explanation.definitionFit: An order form is the paper a customer fills in and sends to a supplier to buy goods.
